transcript: John Proctor Is The Villain absolutely shocked me. With this Broadway season already stacked with so many great new plays, I just didn't expect yet another one that I could see being Tony-worthy. But simply put, this is fantastic theater. John Proctor Is The Villain by Kimberly Belflower and directed by Danya Taymor is about a group of high schoolers in rural Georgia studying The Crucible and coming into their own ideas about feminism and personal agency. Throughout the play, various events occur and secrets are revealed, making the themes of their literature curriculum way too close for comfort. You don't need to have read the crucible to enjoy this piece — it’s more of a framework to activate these characters and their specific story. This play is extremely well-paced and well-sequenced, allowing the flow of information and the establishment of characters to be as efficient as possible. The play's efficiency is also what unleashes a potency in its humor, its urgency, and its catharsis. The performances are great — Sadie Sink is billed above the title, and she certainly has a pivotal role in the story, but everyone in this cast is outstanding and this is a wonderful showcase of ensemble work. Even if you don't think you're in the target audience for this piece, it is so worth seeing. It’s rare to see such strong writing, directing, and performances all in perfect alignment with one another. I apologize to everyone's wallets, but I think this is another must-see. With that, another playbill for my collection.
